article.author: Jon Hamilton
article.title: GLP-1s have transformed weight loss and diabetes. Is addiction next?
article.description: A large study found that people taking GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic for diabetes were less likely to be diagnosed with substance use disorder.
article.content: There's new evidence that GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic can reduce the risk of addiction. A study of more than 600,000 veterans found that those who started taking a GLP-1 drug for diabetes were about 15% less likely to be diagnosed with a substance use disorder. [+4452 chars]

article.author: Sarah Klein
article.title: Mediterranean Diet Linked to Lower Risk of Heart Disease
article.description: New research confirms that adherence to the Mediterranean diet significantly reduces the risk of cardiovascular events in adults over 50.
article.content: Researchers followed more than 25,000 participants over a decade and found those who closely followed the Mediterranean diet had a 28% lower risk of heart disease. The diet emphasizes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and healthy fats. [+3100 chars]

article.author: Rachael Ajmera
article.title: 7 Science-Backed Benefits of Intermittent Fasting
article.description: From weight loss to improved brain function, intermittent fasting has a growing body of evidence supporting its health benefits.
article.content: Intermittent fasting involves cycling between periods of eating and fasting. Studies show it can help reduce inflammation, lower blood sugar, and even extend lifespan in animal models. [+2800 chars]

article.author: Mayo Clinic Staff
article.title: Mental Health and Exercise: What's the Connection?
article.description: Regular physical activity can ease symptoms of depression and anxiety, and experts now say it should be a standard part of mental health treatment.
article.content: Exercise releases endorphins, which naturally improve mood. A review of 49 clinical trials found that physical activity reduced depressive symptoms as effectively as antidepressants in mild to moderate cases. [+3500 chars]

article.author: James Gallagher
article.title: Ultra-processed foods linked to early death, major study finds
article.description: People who eat large amounts of ultra-processed foods face a significantly higher risk of premature death, according to research spanning 20 countries.
article.content: The study, published in The Lancet, tracked dietary habits and mortality rates across 20 countries. Those in the highest quartile of ultra-processed food consumption had a 19% higher risk of all-cause mortality. [+4100 chars]
